extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers and readers of Nature Portfolio journals
extracted.subtask_description: Policy/FAQ describing how transparent peer review is implemented for original research papers in a subset of Nature Portfolio journals, including what gets published, consent rules for authors and reviewers, and limits/exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of transparent peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: For all original research papers published in a subset of the Nature Portfolio journals authors can agree to the publication of a peer review file ... Transparent peer review will be offered to all authors of all original research papers submitted to the journals outlined in our peer review policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies only to original research papers in the specified subset of Nature Portfolio journals; authors are offered the option at acceptance to opt in or out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the published peer review file
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review file will contain the full reviewer reports to authors, author rebuttal letters and editorial decision letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items will be published together to provide readers with the reviewer comments, author responses and editorial decisions. The file will not be edited except as needed for redactions (see redaction policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Author opt-in/opt-out timing and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are given the opportunity to opt out of this scheme at the point of acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal will ask authors at acceptance whether they would like to opt in or out; their choice determines whether the peer review file is published for that paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer consent and acceptance implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are informed of this new initiative when invited to review and can decline to review the manuscript if they are not comfortable with their review being published. Acceptance to review is regarded as permission to release the reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should decide when invited whether they are willing to have their report published; if they accept to review, that acceptance is treated as consent to publication of their report (subject to anonymity choices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity and signing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless reviewers sign the comments to the authors with their name, we will respect and maintain their full anonymity under all circumstances. However, reviewers can request that their name be added to their comments at any point, up to and including receipt of a notification that the manuscript has been accepted in principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may sign their reports to be identified; otherwise names are withheld. Reviewers can retroactively request to be named up until acceptance-in-principle notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option for confidential comments to the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers also have the option to make confidential comments on the manuscript to the editor, although we would prefer that, in the interest of transparency, this is avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any comments that the authors need to address in revision should be made in the ‘comments to the authors’ section rather than in confidential comments to the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for manuscripts peer reviewed elsewhere (transfers)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manuscript is transferred from one Nature Portfolio journal to another, reviewer reports are transferred as well. However, these reports and the author responses to them will not be included in the peer review file as they may have been submitted without consent to potential publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the same reviewers subsequently agree to review for the recipient Nature Portfolio journal offering transparent peer review, only their reviewer reports for the recipient journal will be included. Transferred-manuscript instances will be marked up in the peer review file without naming the other journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication editing, redaction, and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review file will not be edited except to redact confidential information or third party material. Authors will be able to suggest redaction of such material for the editor to review. All redactions when made will be noted in the peer review file, including any requested by the author and agreed by the editor. The journal also reserves the right not to publish peer review reports in special cases, for example, where reports contain a lot of confidential clinical information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors review redaction requests; redactions are recorded in the file. In exceptional circumstances the journal may withhold publication of peer review reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of transparent peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The published peer review file will provide a reader with insight into expert recommendations that informed the editorial decisions. However, the richness and complexity of editorial debate and decisions will not be apparent as correspondence between authors and editors, reviewer comments made confidentially to editors, and internal discussions between editors will remain confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should understand that the peer review file may not capture confidential feedback or internal editorial reasoning; sometimes a paper may be published against the advice of a reviewer due to confidential input not appearing in the file, and editorial explanations may be added in some files to clarify such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of editorial decision letters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nature Portfolio journals offering transparent peer review will publish the editorial decision letters as part of the peer review file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decision letters are included to show the editors' decisions alongside reviewer reports and author responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and reporting of opt-in/feedback metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: We monitor parameters such as author opt-in rates and feedback from authors, reviewers and readers, and have reported these for Nature Communications to the community in an editorial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher collects and reports data on opt-in uptake and stakeholder feedback to evaluate the initiative; authors/reviewers can expect such monitoring to inform ongoing policy.
